meta.sourceModel: Financing Model v8 (Goodwill-only, retail) + Roudabush survey

thesis.v: ±5.04-acre signalized hard corner on US Route 29 in Ruckersville — Greene County's dominant retail node — with Goodwill as an interested build-to-suit anchor tenant. The location, traffic, and tenant interest are all strong, and the retail-only economics now clear the exit cap (v8 model). The deal still hinges on rezoning the R-1/R-2 land to commercial (B-3), which the County supports in principle but has not guaranteed. Purchase is structured subject to rezoning, which caps downside.

flags.text: Goodwill is an interested anchor tenant, and the County (Jim Frydl, Stephanie Golon) is receptive to commercial rezoning on this frontage.

Retail-only economics now clear the exit cap (v8 model): 8.08% yield-on-cost vs. a 7.5% exit cap (+0.58% spread), levered IRR 12.7%, 1.71x equity multiple — full $1.25M whole-site land basis retained.
Adjacent 'Villages at Terrace Greene' brings 282 new townhomes next door — new rooftops and demand tailwind for retail.
Currently zoned R-1/R-2. Entire deal depends on a discretionary rezoning to B-3; not guaranteed and likely to carry proffers.
Rapidan Service Authority has publicly flagged a water-supply constraint (White Run Reservoir underway). Confirm near-term water/sewer availability and tap fees for this parcel.
VDOT is studying alternative intersection designs on US-29 between Rt 33 and Rt 607 (this corner) — future access/median/turn-lane changes possible.
Villages at Terrace Greene proffered ~$700K toward a Rt 29 → Preddy Creek Rd connector — verify alignment vs. this site's Preddy Creek frontage.
Land-price gap: broker ask ($1.475M/ac) vs. model basis ($1.25M whole-site). A prior deal reportedly fell apart over the seller's attorney — expect friction.

scoreNotes.location: Signalized hard corner on US-29 at Rt 607, next to Sheetz; dominant Ruckersville retail node.
scoreNotes.traffic: ≈28,000 AADT on US-29 (broker); VDOT projects this corridor at/over capacity — very high exposure.
scoreNotes.demographics: Greene County growing +6.9% since 2020; county MHI ≈$89.8K (higher than broker's cited $73.8K). Tertiary market, not dense.
scoreNotes.zoning: R-1/R-2 today; requires rezoning to B-3. County supportive in principle (Mixed-Use Village Center) but approval not guaranteed and likely proffered.
scoreNotes.siteLayout: ±5.04 ac supports a retail pad at the corner, with the remainder held undeveloped; storm-drain easement and 3 existing homes to raze are manageable constraints.
scoreNotes.tenantDemand: Goodwill actively interested as anchor tenant; county growth supports continued retail demand on this corridor.
scoreNotes.rentPotential: Raised to 4: v8 model (retail-only) shows a modestly positive development spread (8.08% YoC vs. 7.5% exit cap, +0.58%). Land basis is the key swing factor — see sensitivity; spread turns negative above ≈$1.4M land cost.
scoreNotes.devCost: Elevated — rezoning cost/time, demo of 3 dwellings, RSA water/sewer capacity + tap fees, possible Preddy Creek connector-road impact.
scoreNotes.exitLiquidity: Single-tenant net-lease is financeable and saleable, but Ruckersville is a tertiary market with a shallower buyer pool.

pencil.v: Per the v8 model (retail-only, Goodwill build-to-suit): a single $168K NNN NOI pad on $2,078,000 total cost (full $1.25M whole-site land + $720K shell + $108K soft costs) yields 8.08% against a 7.5% exit cap — a +0.58% spread, 12.7% levered IRR, 1.71x equity multiple, ≈$117K net development profit. The full whole-site land basis is carried against just this one small pad, so land is the key swing factor — the deal is materially stronger at a lower allocated basis (see land-basis sensitivity in Extras). Still contingent on the B-3 rezoning.

listAsk.v: Broker list ask is $1,475,000 per acre (packet) — for ±5.04 ac that implies ~$7.4M gross. The model's $1.25M land basis is Triangle's working whole-site take-down (≈$248K/ac; combined assessed ≈$1.33M). Pin down acreage acquired and negotiated price before hard money.

extras.label: Deal structure (v8 model)
extras.text: Modeled as a Goodwill build-to-suit, single-tenant NNN: Triangle builds the ~$720K retail shell (6,000 SF at $120/SF) and leases at $28/SF NNN. Full $1.25M whole-site land basis retained (owner will not subdivide). Returns are stabilized — no construction-draw/lease-up timeline modeled.

extras.label: Land-basis sensitivity (v8 model)
extras.text: Yield-on-cost at $500K / $750K / $1.0M / $1.25M / $1.5M land cost: 12.65% / 10.65% / 9.19% / 8.08% / 7.22% (development spread +5.15% / +3.15% / +1.69% / +0.58% / −0.28%). Land basis is the key swing factor — spread turns negative above ≈$1.4M.

extras.label: Model corrections applied (v6→v7)
extras.text: The base template carried structural bugs, now fixed: loan-payoff sign error (ending balance now $0), a project-cost double-count (now ties to $5.33M base), and a broken GP reference. Exit broker commission is intentionally kept out of the project IRR (treated as separate take-home). Some items still pending Ben/Conor confirmation.

extras.label: FLU place-type amendment
extras.text: Broker notes a Future Land Use map amendment adding a Technology/Flex Research & Development place type (~550 additional acres) in the area.

extras.label: Regional context
extras.text: Greene County is within the Charlottesville MSA; ~20 min N of downtown Charlottesville, ~100 mi SW of Washington, DC; a gateway to Shenandoah National Park.

extras.label: Water infrastructure
extras.text: Greene County approved a reduced-scope White Run Reservoir (600 MG storage, 2 MGD treatment, ~$65.5M) on 6/24/2025 — long-term capacity is being built, but near-term availability must be confirmed with RSA.
